Of the approximately 5,000 flowering plants that grow in the Northeast, about 20 per cent are aliens. This means that, as far as is known, these plants were not here when the European settlers arrived, but they had some help getting here.

Most of the plants were either brought deliberately to be grown for food, medicine or beauty. Others probably hitchhiked as seeds in loads of hay or on rocks used for ballast.

TIANANMEN Square. Relations between the United States and China have since chilled considerably, and Congress has sought to show its disapproval of the Communist Government's violent crackdown through various diplomatic sanctions.

headline:
ART;
Prints Tell the Story of the Mexican Revolution
abstract:
MEXICO has been on the minds of New York museum- and gallery-goers for several months. Its rich and vivid art certainly represents a contrast to the spare and heady work that has come to exemplify New York art. At the Bronx Museum is another contrast: In place of splendors from Mexico we have crisp documentary history. 

The Mexican Revolution, which was a long-term and lurching struggle with many phases going back to the mid-19th century, is the subject of the exhibition. The issues surrounding the conflict were basic and raw, the poor against the rich, and the story is told in a fitting and direct way through prints, the great majority of them wood or linoleum block prints made by the members of "El Taller de Graffica Popular."
